thumb.title: India drew in Wellington. Their batters climbed.

concept: A ladder post. The story is movement, not a result, so the design is built around climbing. The hero sets the draw in muted grey and the real takeaway in white: India's batters still won the week. Slide 2 is a 'places gained' bar chart where the one lit bar is Padikkal's +15, the biggest jump, with every batter's score and new rank underneath. Slide 3 strips the top 10 down to three numbers, 6 · 7 · 9, the spots Pant, Gill and Jaiswal now hold. Slide 4 gives Bumrah his own '=2nd' and gives New Zealand's climbers a fair line. The last slide points at the Hagley Oval decider and asks who climbs next. Cricket blue, type and charts only: no player photos, no logos.
caption:
The Wellington Test was a draw. India's batters still won the week.

The new ICC Test rankings are out and five Indian batters moved up after their 720/9 declared.

Pant is up to 6th after his 128. Gill is 7th after 98. Jaiswal jumps five places into the top 10 at 9th. KL Rahul's 136 lifts him to 25th and Padikkal's 80 is worth 15 places.

Bumrah's five wickets take him up three spots to joint second among Test bowlers. New Zealand climbed too: Glenn Phillips is at a career-best 17th and Henry Nicholls is up 10 to 30th.

The series decider starts at Hagley Oval in Christchurch on November 26.
